question_html: Which of the following errors does NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?

options.A: Wrong casting of subsidiary books
options.B: Error of complete omission
options.C: Posting an amount on the wrong side of an account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Errors of complete omission do not affect the trial balance because both debit and credit aspects are omitted equally[cite: 12].
topic_text: Types of Errors and Effect on Trial Balance

question_html: Treating the purchase of an office typewriter as an ordinary office expense is an example of which type of error?

options.A: Error of commission
options.B: Error of principle

answer_html: Answer: (B) When a transaction is recorded in contravention of accounting principles, like treating capital expenditure as revenue, it is an error of principle[cite: 12].

question_html: What is opened to artificially make a trial balance agree when a difference exists due to errors?

options.A: Trading Account
options.B: Suspense Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) A Suspense Account is opened to temporarily accommodate the difference in the trial balance[cite: 12].
topic_text: Suspense Account and Rectification After Trial Balance

question_html: Which account is opened to rectify errors relating to nominal accounts (expenses and incomes) discovered in the next accounting period, in order to avoid falsifying current profit?

options.A: Suspense Account
options.B: Profit and Loss Adjustment Account (Prior Period Items)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Correction of nominal accounts in the next period should be through a special account styled as 'Profit and Loss Adjustment Account' or 'Prior Period Items'[cite: 12].
topic_text: Correction in the Next Accounting Period

question_html: Goods worth ₹100 taken by the proprietor for domestic use were incorrectly credited to Sales Account. What type of error is this?

options.A: Error of Principle
options.B: Error of Commission

answer_html: Answer: (B) Posting or recording in the wrong account or wrong side constitutes an error of commission[cite: 12].

question_html: If the trial balance debit column exceeds the credit column by ₹150, what was the initial balance put into the Suspense Account to make it tally?

options.A: Credited with ₹150
options.B: Debited with ₹150
options.D: Carried forward to next year as asset

answer_html: Answer: (A) If debit exceeds credit, the suspense account is credited with the difference to equalize the trial balance columns[cite: 12].

question_html: Which of the following errors will cause the trial balance NOT to agree?

options.A: Complete omission of a credit sale transaction
options.B: Posting an amount to the wrong account but on the correct side
options.C: Wrong casting of the Sales Book
options.D: Recording purchase of machinery as purchases

answer_html: Answer: (C) Wrong casting of subsidiary books affects trial balance agreement, whereas complete omission or wrong account posting on correct side do not[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the correct debit when wages are paid to workmen for erecting a new machine in the factory?

options.A: Wages Account
options.B: Machine Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Expenses incurred for the erection of a machine are capital expenditure and must be debited to the Machine Account[cite: 12].
topic_text: Capital vs Revenue Expenditure / Errors of Principle

question_html: If the effect of errors committed cancels out mutually without affecting the trial balance total, they are called:

options.A: Errors of Principle
options.B: Compensating Errors

answer_html: Answer: (B) Compensating errors occur when the effect of errors committed cancels out each other[cite: 12].

question_html: How should repairs made to second-hand machinery purchased recently be treated upon acquisition?

options.A: Debited to Repairs Account
options.B: Debited to Machinery Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount spent on repairs of old/second-hand furniture or machinery upon purchase is capital expenditure, debited to the asset account[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the correct treatment when ₹200 is received from Smith whose account was previously written off as a bad debt?

options.A: Credited to Smith's personal account
options.B: Credited to Bad Debts Recovered Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Recovery of bad debts previously written off is credited to Bad Debts Recovered Account[cite: 12].

question_html: Goods worth ₹50 given as charity should be credited to which account?

options.A: Charity Account
options.B: Sales Account

answer_html: Answer: (C) Goods given away as charity or free samples are credited to Purchase Account because stock goes out at cost[cite: 12].

question_html: When should errors be corrected by overwriting according to standard accounting practices?

options.A: Always
options.B: Never

answer_html: Answer: (B) Errors should never be corrected by overwriting; corrections must be made by appropriate rectification entries or statements[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the primary purpose of preparing a trial balance?

options.A: To locate all errors of principle
options.B: To check the arithmetical accuracy of the journal and ledger accounts

answer_html: Answer: (B) Trial balance is prepared to check the arithmetical accuracy of journal and ledger accounts[cite: 12].

question_html: If rent paid to the landlord of the proprietor's private residence is debited to Rent Account, it is an example of:

options.A: Error of Commission
options.B: Error of Principle / Personal Drawings Misclassified

answer_html: Answer: (B) Rent for proprietor's residence is personal drawings, and debiting rent account is an error of principle / wrong account classification[cite: 12].

question_html: Goods purchased from A for ₹10,000 were passed through the Sales Book. What is the impact of this error on gross profit?

options.A: Increase in gross profit
options.B: Decrease in gross profit

answer_html: Answer: (A) Passing purchases through sales book understates purchases (increasing gross profit) and overstates sales (further increasing gross profit), resulting in an increase in gross profit[cite: 12].

question_html: If a purchase return of ₹1,000 has been wrongly posted to the debit of the Sales Returns Account, but correctly entered in the supplier's account, how will the trial balance be affected?

options.A: Debit side will exceed credit side by ₹1,000
options.B: Credit side will exceed debit side by ₹1,000
options.C: Debit side of the trial balance will be ₹2,000 more than the credit side

answer_html: Answer: (C) Purchase return should have been credited. Instead, supplier is credited correctly, but sales return is debited erroneously (instead of purchase return credit). This causes a double debit discrepancy of ₹2,000[cite: 12].

question_html: What are 'Prior Period Items' as per accounting standards referred to in Chapter 6?

options.A: Income or expenses arising in the current period as a result of errors or omissions in the preparation of financial statements of one or more prior periods
options.B: Future anticipated revenues
options.C: Tax provisions for the current year

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prior period items are material income or expenses arising in the current period due to errors or omissions in prior period financial statements[cite: 12].
topic_text: Prior Period Items and Next Period Corrections

question_html: When errors are detected before the preparation of the trial balance, how are errors affecting only one account rectified?

options.A: Through complete journal entries involving suspense account
options.B: Through rectification statements or direct entries on the appropriate side of the concerned account
options.C: By opening a profit and loss adjustment account
options.D: They cannot be rectified until next year

answer_html: Answer: (B) Errors affecting one side of an account before trial balance are corrected by making rectification statements/entries in the appropriate side of the concerned account[cite: 12].

question_html: If the purchase account was overcast by ₹10,000 in the previous year and discovered in the next year, how is it rectified using the Profit and Loss Adjustment Account?

options.A: Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c Dr. 10,000 To Suspense A/c 10,000
options.B: Suspense A/c Dr. 10,000 To Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c 10,000
options.C: Purchases A/c Dr. 10,000 To Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c 10,000

answer_html: Answer: (B) Overcast of purchases in the previous year requires crediting Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c to rectify prior period profit[cite: 12].
topic_text: Correction in Next Accounting Period / P&L Adjustment

question_html: What is the effect on the trial balance if a credit sale of ₹1,470 is debited to a customer account at ₹1,740?

options.A: Debit side of trial balance is in excess by ₹270
options.B: Credit side of trial balance is in excess by ₹270

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debiting ₹1,740 instead of ₹1,470 creates an excess debit of ₹270 ($1,740 - $1,470), causing the trial balance debit side to exceed credit by ₹270[cite: 12].

question_html: If the Sales Book is cast short by ₹900, how does it affect the ledger and trial balance?

options.A: Sales Account is credited short by ₹900; trial balance credit total is ₹900 short
options.B: Sales Account is debited by ₹900

answer_html: Answer: (A) Undercasting of sales book means sales account is credited short by ₹900, making the trial balance credit total ₹900 short[cite: 12].

question_html: When rectifying errors after the preparation of the trial balance, why can't certain one-sided errors be corrected without a Suspense Account?

options.A: Because double entry requires both debit and credit aspects, and one-sided errors leave an unallocated discrepancy accounted for by the suspense account.
options.B: Because ICAI rules prohibit it.
options.D: Because ledger accounts cannot be reopened.

answer_html: Answer: (A) One-sided errors affect only one account, so completing a journal entry requires taking the difference to the Suspense Account[cite: 12].

question_html: If a scooter purchased for ₹3,000 was debited to the conveyance account instead of Motor Vehicles Account, and 10% depreciation applies, what is the rectified capitalised asset value?
answer_html: Answer: (B) As shown in Illustration 8, capitalisation of scooter is ₹3,000 less 10% depreciation ($3,000 - $300) = ₹2,700[cite: 12].

question_html: A sale of ₹200 to Singh & Co. was correctly entered in the sales book but wrongly credited to their account. What is the rectifying entry if a suspense account is used?

options.A: Singh & Co. Dr. 400 To Suspense A/c 400
options.B: Suspense A/c Dr. 200 To Singh & Co. 200
options.C: Singh & Co. Dr. 200 To Sales A/c 200
options.D: Sales A/c Dr. 200 To Singh & Co. 200

answer_html: Answer: (A) To remove wrong credit (200) and give correct debit (200), Singh & Co. must be debited by ₹400, with suspense credited by ₹400[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect on net profit if an accrual of ₹560 for telephone charges has been completely omitted?

options.A: Net profit is overstated by ₹560
options.B: Net profit is understated by ₹560

answer_html: Answer: (A) Omitting an expense accrual results in expenses being understated, which overstates net profit[cite: 12].
topic_text: Effect of Errors on Net Profit

question_html: If goods worth ₹1,000 were sent on sale or return basis to a customer and incorrectly entered as actual sales at the close of the year (cost ₹800, margin 25% on cost), what is the adjustment required to profit?

options.A: Profit decreased by ₹200 (markup amount)
options.B: Profit increased by ₹1,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) Recording approval sales as actual sales overstates sales and profit by the profit margin (₹200), requiring a reduction in profit[cite: 12].
topic_text: Sale or Return Basis and Profit Impact

question_html: Which step is NOT part of the recommended procedure to locate errors when a trial balance does not agree?

options.A: Halving the difference to check if a balance was written in the wrong column
options.B: Checking the casting of subsidiary books
options.C: Writing off the difference directly to capital without investigation

answer_html: Answer: (C) Writing off differences without investigation is incorrect; errors leading to differences must be located and rectified[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the correct rectifying entry for a credit sale of ₹200 to Mr. Ghanshyam that was wrongly posted to the debit of Mr. Radheshyam as ₹20 (without suspense)?

options.A: Mr. Ghanshyam Dr. 200 To Mr. Radheshyam 20 To Suspense 180
options.B: Mr. Radheshyam Dr. 200 To Mr. Ghanshyam 200
options.C: Sales A/c Dr. 200 To Mr. Radheshyam 200
options.D: Suspense A/c Dr. 200 To Mr. Ghanshyam 200

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Illustration 7, Ghanshyam needs debit of 200, Radheshyam's wrong debit of 20 must be reversed by credit, and the remaining 180 goes to suspense[cite: 12].

question_html: If tools bought for ₹1,200 were inadvertently debited to purchases, how is it rectified before preparing annual accounts?

options.A: Loose Tools A/c Dr. 1,200 To Purchases A/c 1,200
options.B: Purchases A/c Dr. 1,200 To Loose Tools A/c 1,200
options.C: Suspense A/c Dr. 1,200 To Purchases A/c 1,200

answer_html: Answer: (A) Capital items (tools) debited to purchases must be rectified by debiting Loose Tools Account and crediting Purchases Account[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect of an unposted total of Bills Receivable Book amounting to ₹1,500 on the trial balance?

options.A: Trial balance debit total is short by ₹1,500
options.B: Trial balance credit total is short by ₹1,500

answer_html: Answer: (A) Leaving the total of Bills Receivable Book unposted means the debit side of the ledger/trial balance is short by ₹1,500[cite: 12].

question_html: How is a return of ₹90 to Shyam Sunder posted as ₹9 in his account rectified?

options.A: Debit Shyam Sunder's account by ₹81
options.B: Credit Shyam Sunder's account by ₹81

answer_html: Answer: (A) Shyam Sunder was credited short by ₹81 ($90 - $9) in posting a return to him (which should be debited/reduced in his account), hence his account needs a debit of ₹81[cite: 12].

question_html: If a vehicle bought originally for ₹7,000 and depreciated to ₹1,200 is sold for ₹1,500 without entries (other than bank), what is the profit on sale of vehicle?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Sale price ₹1,500 minus book value ₹1,200 = ₹300 profit on sale of vehicle[cite: 12].

question_html: What happens when a credit sale of ₹120 to Ramesh is wrongly passed through the Purchase Book?

options.A: Purchases and Ramesh are both debited incorrectly
options.B: Ramesh must be debited by ₹240 and Purchases/Sales credited to rectify

answer_html: Answer: (B) Passing sale through purchase book debits purchase instead of Ramesh, requiring Ramesh to be debited by ₹240 (to reverse wrong entry and record correct debt) with corresponding credits[cite: 12].

question_html: How is an unrecorded credit purchase of goods worth ₹100 from Mohan Narain rectified?

options.A: Purchases A/c Dr. 100 To Mohan Narain 100
options.B: Mohan Narain Dr. 100 To Purchases A/c 100
options.C: Suspense A/c Dr. 100 To Mohan Narain 100

answer_html: Answer: (A) Complete omission of a credit purchase is recorded by debiting Purchases Account and crediting Mohan Narain[cite: 12].

question_html: If freight paid on a machine (₹5,600) was incorrectly posted to the Freight Account as ₹6,500 instead of being capitalised, what is the machine account correction before depreciation?

options.A: Machine A/c Dr. ₹5,600
options.B: Machine A/c Dr. ₹6,500

answer_html: Answer: (A) The actual freight paid and capitalised is ₹5,600[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect of an error where a return of ₹120 from Mukesh was posted to his debit instead of credit?

options.A: Mukesh's account is debited short by ₹240
options.B: Trial balance is unaffected
options.C: Mukesh's account must be credited by ₹240 to rectify

answer_html: Answer: (C) To remove wrong debit (120) and provide correct credit (120), Mukesh's account must be credited with ₹240[cite: 12].
topic_text: Wrong Side Posting in Personal Accounts

question_html: If goods amounting to ₹100 returned by a customer were taken into inventory but omitted from the books, what is the rectifying entry?

options.A: Returns Inward A/c Dr. 100 To Debtors A/c 100
options.B: Debtors A/c Dr. 100 To Returns Inward A/c 100
options.C: Trading A/c Dr. 100 To Inventory A/c 100
options.D: Suspense A/c Dr. 100 To Returns Inward A/c 100

answer_html: Answer: (A) Omission of customer returns is rectified by debiting Returns Inward Account and crediting Debtors Account[cite: 12].

question_html: How is a payment of ₹215 to Mohammad Sadiq posted to his credit as ₹125 rectified?

options.A: Mohammad Sadiq's account should be debited by ₹90
options.B: Mohammad Sadiq's account should be debited by ₹340
options.C: Mohammad Sadiq's account should be credited by ₹90

answer_html: Answer: (B) Payment requires debiting Mohammad Sadiq by ₹215. Crediting him by ₹125 created a wrong credit. To clear the wrong credit (125) and give correct debit (215), total debit needed is $215 + 125 = ₹340$[cite: 12].

question_html: If a sale of ₹2,300 to Mr. Lala was posted to the credit of Mrs. Mala, what is the rectifying entry using suspense?

options.A: Mrs. Mala Dr. 2,300, Mr. Lala Dr. 2,300 To Suspense A/c 4,600
options.B: Mr. Lala Dr. 2,300 To Mrs. Mala 2,300
options.C: Suspense A/c Dr. 4,600 To Lala To Mala

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Illustration 3 of Practical Questions, Mrs. Mala is debited to cancel wrong credit (2300), Mr. Lala is debited to record correct sale (2300), and Suspense is credited with 4,600[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect on trial balance of a purchase return day book correctly entered at ₹6,160 but not posted to the ledger?

options.A: Trial balance credit side is short by ₹6,160
options.B: Trial balance debit side is short by ₹6,160

answer_html: Answer: (A) Failure to post purchase return total to the ledger leaves the return outward account uncredited, making the credit side short by ₹6,160[cite: 12].

question_html: If a bad debt of ₹1,560 had not been written off and provision for doubtful debts is maintained at 10% of trade receivables (ledger balance ₹23,390 with opening provision ₹2,320), what is the new provision amount?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Trade receivables after writing off bad debt = $23,390 - 1,560 = ₹21,560; 10% of this is ₹2,156[cite: 12].

question_html: When cash received from C. Dass (₹620) is posted to the debit of G. Dass, how is it rectified using suspense?

options.A: Suspense A/c Dr. 1,240 To C. Dass 620 To G. Dass 620
options.B: C. Dass Dr. 620, G. Dass Dr. 620 To Suspense 1,240
options.C: G. Dass Dr. 620 To C. Dass 620

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Illustration 4 of Practical Questions, suspense is debited by 1,240 to clear errors and credit both parties correctly[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect on profit if a purchase amount of ₹2,395 was wrongly posted as ₹2,593 in the previous accounting period?

options.A: Profit was understated by ₹198 in the previous period
options.B: Profit was overstated by ₹198

answer_html: Answer: (A) Purchases were over-debited by ₹198 ($2,593 - $2,395), which understated the previous period's profit[cite: 12].

question_html: If a credit sale of ₹50 has been credited to Sales and also credited to Trade Receivables Account, how is it rectified?

options.A: Trade Receivables A/c Dr. 50 To Suspense A/c 50
options.B: Sales A/c Dr. 50 To Trade Receivables 50
options.C: Suspense A/c Dr. 50 To Trade Receivables 50

answer_html: Answer: (A) Trade receivables should have been debited by ₹50. Instead, it was credited. To remove wrong credit and give correct debit, Trade Receivables must be debited by ₹100? Wait, checking source: Trade Receivables A/c Dr. 100 To Suspense? Let's verify source text: 'Trade receivables Account Dr. 100 To Suspense Account'[cite: 12].

question_html: When discounts received (₹1,320) had been debited to discounts allowed, what is the rectifying entry?

options.A: Suspense A/c Dr. 2,640 To Discount Allowed A/c 1,320 To Discount Received A/c 1,320
options.B: Discount Allowed Dr. 1,320 To Discount Received 1,320
options.C: Suspense A/c Dr. 1,320 To Discount Allowed 1,320

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Practical Question 1, clearing wrong debit of discount allowed (1320) and providing correct credit (1320), plus correct credit of discount received (1320), requires Suspense debit of ₹2,640[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the correct accounting treatment when goods worth ₹1,960 are withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use and no entry has been made?

options.A: Drawings A/c Dr. 1,960 To Purchases A/c 1,960
options.B: Purchases A/c Dr. 1,960 To Drawings A/c 1,960
options.C: Capital A/c Dr. 1,960 To Sales A/c 1,960

answer_html: Answer: (A) Proprietor's withdrawal of goods for personal use requires debiting Drawings Account and crediting Purchases Account at cost[cite: 12].

question_html: If a supplier's account is overcast by ₹225, how does it affect the trial balance and how is it rectified with suspense?

options.A: Supplier A/c Dr. 225 To Suspense A/c 225
options.B: Suspense A/c Dr. 225 To Supplier A/c 225

answer_html: Answer: (A) Overcast of credit balance (supplier account) means credit is excess, so debiting the supplier account by ₹225 and crediting suspense rectifies it[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the effect on profit if a sale of ₹573 was entered in the Sales Book as ₹753 and posted to the credit of the customer?

options.A: Profit is overstated by ₹180
options.B: Profit is understated by ₹180

answer_html: Answer: (A) Sales book overstated by $753 - 573 = ₹180, which overstates sales and profit by ₹180[cite: 12].

question_html: If a purchase of ₹420 from Mantri & Co. was passed through the Sales Day Book as ₹240, what is the rectifying entry after final accounts using Profit & Loss Adjustment Account?

options.A: Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c Dr. 660 To Mantri & Co. 660
options.B: Mantri & Co. Dr. 660 To Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c 660
options.C: Purchases A/c Dr. 420 To Sales A/c 240 To Mantri 180

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Chapter 6 (Practical Question 5), after final accounts, nominal accounts are routed through Profit & Loss Adjustment A/c ($420 + 240 = ₹660$) credited to Mantri & Co[cite: 12].
topic_text: Final Accounts Rectification via P&L Adjustment
